empty/full is the clean L1 opposite; exit, stale, plentiful, entrance are not. Gloss stays hidden. Both rounds pass.

fondness ~ liking (a liking for something); jealousy, derision, animosity run the other way and acceptance is different. Gloss is close to the shared sense. Both rounds pass.

Overrule R1's fail. Agree with R1. contempt = disdain is sound and insult, acceptance, affront are not feelings of scorn, but the gloss shown is garbled ('...unworthy of or beneath one scorn') and defines disdain with the clue word itself. Hide it; the link and options are fine.

Agree with R1. legacy = inheritance (the thing handed down) is sound and claimant, eyewitness, landowner are people, but the gloss is inheritance's 'hereditary succession' sense (the act of succeeding), not the property inherited that matches legacy. Hide it.

Agree with R1. At L2 (age ~9) range = scope only in the abstract 'extent' sense, and scope, threshold and infrared are well above that level; 'width' is also arguable for range's extent/span sense. Dropping width would not fix the level problem, and the gloss ends in a stray colon. Doubtful, so it does not ship.

story = narrative; memoir, biography, fantasy are kinds of writing, not synonyms. Gloss right. Both rounds pass.

Agree with R1. Nutmeg is a spice and parsley, almond, coconut, soy are not categories it belongs to, but the gloss shown is spice's 'used as a preservative' sense rather than the flavouring sense a child needs. Hide it.

beauty -> beautiful noun-to-adjective family; magical, heroic, natural, joyful are other roots. Gloss right. Both rounds pass.

proclaim = declare; accuse, invoke, condemn are not. Gloss right. Both rounds pass.
plane = airplane; meridian, perimeter (geometry senses) and airship (a different aircraft) are not. Gloss right. Both rounds pass.

Agree with R2. Thesauruses list soot as a synonym of grime (grimy black dirt), so soot is a second defensible answer, and dropping it would leave only silt, below the two-option minimum. Cannot be rescued.

just -> justice is the adjective-to-noun family (the gloss says 'being just or fair'); extra, end, letter, plus are unrelated, so it is solvable even for a child who reads 'just' as the adverb. Both rounds pass.

dusk = twilight; dawn is the other end of the day, meadow and lagoon unrelated. Gloss right. Both rounds pass.
